tables.how: Each contract-approval notice names the contractor’s board members and top officers. Every itemized contribution since 2017 from a person with the same first and last name is taken when it went to a committee carrying the approving officer’s surname, or to a supervisor’s committee where the Board approved, and is dated from 180 days before to 365 days after the approval. That gives 773 matches by name. Only the 53 in which the donor’s stated employer is also the contractor are listed, because a name alone can belong to two people; the other 720 are counted and not listed. The rows add up to $13,400.
tables.limits: No row is a finding that a donation broke the law. A match of name and employer makes it likely, not certain, that the donor is the officer on the notice; it is not confirmed. The ban applies only to contracts worth $100,000 or more in a fiscal year and runs from the day a proposal was submitted, which the notices do not give: 180 days before approval is a stand-in. Nonprofit leaders are often active in local politics and give small sums on their own account. Whether a committee later returned a donation was not checked. A donor who gave to two committees, or whose organization had two approvals, has a row for each.
